title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: STRENGTHENING OF CPGRAMS
body_text:
The Government has undertaken several measures to strengthen the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS). Major reforms include adoption of next-generation technologies to enhance system capabilities, introduction of the Grievance Redressal Assessment and Index (GRAI) to benchmark the performance of Ministries and Departments, publication of monthly CPGRAMS reports for transparency and monitoring, capacity building of grievance officers through Sevottam, integration with the grievance portals of Central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs, multilingual grievance registration and translation facility through integration with Bhashini, operationalization of the Feedback Call Centre, availability of CPGRAMS through the mobile application and Common Service Centres (CSCs), reduction of prescribed grievance disposal timeline from 30 days to 21 days, and launch of 'Samadhan Didi', an AI-powered multilingual voice-first chatbot for grievance registration.
Further, to improve the quality of grievance redressal, the Comprehensive Guidelines on Handling of Public Grievances, issued in August 2024, mandates establishment of dedicated Grievance Cells in Ministries/Departments, appointment of experienced nodal officers, monitoring of pendency and citizen feedback, emphasis on root cause analysis, and strengthened escalation mechanisms. In addition, a dedicated Review Meeting Module has been operationalised in CPGRAMS to facilitate senior-level review of public grievances to further improve the efficiency and quality of grievance redressal.
The details of grievances received, disposed of, pending, and the average disposal time during the last three years on CPGRAMS in respect of grievances pertaining to Central Ministries/Departments are as under:
Year Brought Forward Receipt Disposal Pending Average Disposal Time (Centre) 2023-24 74,217 17,37,599 17,05,792 1,06,024 16 2024-25 1,06,024 16,73,645 17,17,570 62,099 15 2025-26 62,099 18,33,972 18,12,923 83,148 14
CPGRAMS is amongst the early digital platforms to use AI/ ML enabled dashboards which helped in extensive data analysis towards exploratory and predictive insights for root cause analysis through categorisation by priority, repeat and spam, geographical analysis of grievances, trend analysis and semantic search. Building on this foundation, the Government is developing NextGen CPGRAMS as an end-to-end digital public grievance platform leveraging emerging technologies, including AI/ML, to further enhance citizen experience and improve grievance redressal system.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.
*****
NKR/AV

ministry.name: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed measures taken to strengthen CPGRAMS, including the Grievance Redressal Assessment Index (GRAI), Bhashini-based multilingual support, the 'Samadhan Didi' AI chatbot, reduction of disposal timeline from 30 to 21 days, and a Review Meeting Module for senior-level oversight. Data shared showed that in 2025-26, over 18.3 lakh grievances were received and 18.1 lakh disposed of, with average disposal time improving to 14 days from 16 days in 2023-24. The Government also issued Comprehensive Guidelines on Handling of Public Grievances in August 2024 and is developing 'NextGen CPGRAMS' using AI/ML for further improvement.
enrichment.context:
CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System) is the online platform through which citizens can lodge grievances against any Central Ministry/Department or State/UT for redressal. It functions under the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, and is a key instrument of India's governance reform agenda aimed at citizen-centric administration, transparency, and accountability. Over the years, CPGRAMS has evolved from a simple grievance-logging tool into an AI/ML-enabled analytics platform capable of root-cause analysis, spam/repeat detection, and predictive insights—positioning it as a model for e-governance and Digital India initiatives.

The reforms mentioned—GRAI for ranking ministries, Sevottam training for grievance officers, integration with Bhashini for multilingual access, and the AI chatbot 'Samadhan Didi'—reflect a broader push to use emerging technologies for improving service delivery, consistent with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission's recommendations on grievance redressal and the government's Minimum Government, Maximum Governance philosophy. The shrinking of the disposal timeline (30 to 21 days) and declining average disposal time (16 to 14 days) indicate incremental efficiency gains, though the volume of grievances has also risen sharply (from about 17.4 lakh in 2023-24 to over 18.3 lakh in 2025-26), underscoring persistent demand for responsive grievance redressal mechanisms. The planned 'NextGen CPGRAMS' signals continued institutional investment in AI-driven governance tools for public grievance management.

prelims_questions.question: CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System) functions under which of the following?
options: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
prelims_questions.explanation: CPGRAMS is administered by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, as reflected in the release which cites the Minister of State PMO/Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions responding on CPGRAMS.

prelims_questions.question: As per recent government reforms, the prescribed timeline for grievance disposal under CPGRAMS has been reduced from 30 days to how many days?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that the prescribed grievance disposal timeline has been reduced from 30 days to 21 days as part of CPGRAMS reforms.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of technology-driven reforms such as AI/ML integration and multilingual chatbots in strengthening public grievance redressal mechanisms in India. Illustrate with reference to CPGRAMS.
